plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with layered petals and bright golden centers. They bring color to gardens at the coldest time of year, when most other plants are dormant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late December through March, depending on the variety, so mid-January is within the season.
plants.location: Temperate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere, including the southeastern and Pacific Coast United States, where it is a classic winter bloomer. It is native to Japan, Korea and eastern China.
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of Camellia sinensis, the plant that gives us tea. In Japan the camellia (tsubaki) has long been a symbol of winter.
